chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"When you buy something from goods or otherwise, say Allahu Akbar, then say: 'O Allah, I have bought it seeking Your bounty from it, so make bounty in it. O Allah, I have bought it seeking Your provision from it, so make provision for me in it.' Then repeat [this supplication] over each item three times."

key_terms.فَضْلٍ: bounty, grace, or surplus blessing from God
key_terms.مَتَاعٍ: goods, merchandise, or items of use

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and etiquette when buying goods in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a spiritual framework for commerce, transforming mundane transactions into acts of worship by seeking divine blessing (*fadl*) and sustenance (*rizq*) in material goods. The instruction to repeat the supplication three times reflects the Shia emphasis on *thawab* (reward) through consistent dhikr, ensuring the buyer remains mindful of Allah’s provision amidst daily economic activities. This practice aligns with the broader Shia tradition of sanctifying everyday actions, turning trade into a means of drawing closer to God rather than mere profit-seeking.
